PullRequest.Title: github: add reusable repository queries
PullRequest.Body:
Related microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9678.

- Add reusable one-shot repository metadata and explicitly paged repository listing/search to the shared GitHub domain, using neutral account/repository references.
- Retain server-provided HTTPS/SSH clone URLs and expose search totals, incomplete results and the 1,000-result ceiling. Validate pagination before dispatch; fetch only one page per call so query scoping, selection and operation budgets remain caller-owned.
- Reuse existing credential/account checks, endpoint routing, governed REST transport, private ETags, request sharing and cancellation.
- Add 24 real-engine/fake-transport contract cases and update the source-adjacent README/client inventory with concrete consumer evidence.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed request sets `etag: true`; `GitHubTransport` keys cache entries by the complete URL and retains the decoded response body in a 500-entry LRU, while search results can contain 100 full repository objects. The documented target consumers are type-ahead repository pickers, and the existing remote-source picker dispatches successive distinct queries after a 300 ms debounce. Exact concurrent requests remain coalesced even with ETags disabled. The exact retained byte total depends on result density and session usage, affecting severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: decoded JSON response strings and LRU cache entry objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retention grows with the number of distinct successful query/page URLs, up to 500 entries per authorized client; bytes per entry grow with repository-result count (up to 100) and metadata size.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: retained memory and increased GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, the shared GitHub query service had no arbitrary repository-search route, so changing repository-picker text could not populate its long-lived transport cache with distinct search result bodies.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Repository search now stores each successful, ETagged search response body under its full URL (including arbitrary `q`, page, sort, and order) in the client transport's shared LRU.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `searchRepositories` request at RIGHT line 563 opts every `/search/repositories?q=...&page=...` response into transport ETag caching; this search endpoint and its arbitrary query/page key space did not exist in the shared query service before this PR.
Findings.Title: Do not retain every distinct repository search response
Findings.Impact: Repeated repository-picker searches retain obsolete full search pages for the lifetime of the authorized client, growing memory and GC pressure as users type different queries or reopen the picker; at the 500-entry cache limit this can retain hundreds of dense 100-repository JSON pages.
Findings.Evidence: `searchRepositories` builds a URL containing the trimmed user query and pagination options, then sets `etag: true`. `GitHubTransport._restCacheKey` includes the full URL, and `_executeRest` stores the complete decoded `body` in `_restCache`, an `LRUCache<string, IRestCacheEntry>(500)` whose limit is entry-count rather than bytes. Thus no two distinct search strings share an entry, and each dense page can retain JSON for up to 100 repository records. The existing intended remote-source consumer invokes search as the quick-pick value changes, so repeated picker use realistically accumulates many large entries for queries unlikely to be repeated.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep exact-request in-flight sharing but disable representation caching for search (`etag: false`), or place search results in a separate short-lived, byte-bounded cache; reserve the existing ETag cache for stable repository/list URLs that are realistically revalidated.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Credential resolution must complete, followed by one repository REST request and JSON mapping; both are on the caller's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the token's GitHub account identity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One `/user` network call per cold credential generation, shared across concurrent credential requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing authorized query operations already used this credential-resolution boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the first authorized repository operation; absent for warm credentials.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One REST request per `getRepository` call, with exact-URL in-flight coalescing and ETag revalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The shared query API previously exposed repository subscriptions but no one-shot metadata operation; subscribed reads already used the same REST URL and transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks completion of the metadata read.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One normalized repository reference per call; concurrent duplicate references collapse to one wire request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exact repository URLs coalesce in `GitHubTransport`; the shared queue caps active requests at 2 per host and 2 per caller (4 globally).
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold client credential resolution coalesces and caches the resolved credential after `/user`; repository metadata then uses the transport's authorization-scoped, 500-entry ETag LRU. Warm exact-URL reads revalidate with the cached ETag and concurrent exact reads coalesce. Failures are not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path, one-request cardinality, coalescing, and queue limits are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository documents vary in size and network latency, but call count and bounded mapping are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new operation performs one necessary network read, shares exact in-flight work and ETags with subscriptions, and adds no collection fan-out.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Credential resolution and exactly one `/user/repos` page must complete. Mapping is synchronous over at most 100 returned repositories.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One `/user` call only for a cold credential generation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Shared authorized operations already paid this once per credential generation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the first page only when credentials are cold.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one `/user/repos` request per API call, serving up to 100 repositories; additional pages require explicit caller calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No shared repository-list operation existed; legacy consumers performed their own one-page REST request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The selected page blocks caller progress; no hidden page draining occurs.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 100 repository records per explicit page call; effective network cardinality is one per distinct requested page after exact-key coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The API does not auto-page. Caller-issued pages are governed by the shared queue's host/caller limits; identical page URLs coalesce.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold credential behavior is as above. Each list URL is ETag-cached by account and full page/options URL; exact repeats coalesce/revalidate. Cache entries are bounded to 500 transport-wide, and errors/empty responses without ETags are not retained.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: pagination validation, one REST call, 100-item cap, and queue concurrency are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users with very large accessible-repository sets may explicitly fetch many pages, but the diff neither loops nor starts those requests itself.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable boundary fan-out: pagination remains caller-owned, mapping is capped at 100 items, and shared concurrency/backpressure apply.

Scenarios.Scenario: Repository search from a type-ahead picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Credential resolution and one `/search/repositories` request must complete, followed by parsing and mapping at most 100 repositories. All are on the picker/search caller's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One `/user` call per cold credential generation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing authorized operations already used this boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks only the first search on a cold client.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Search GitHub repositories for the supplied query and page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One search request per distinct explicit call/page, returning up to 100 full repository records; exact simultaneous duplicates coalesce.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The shared service had no repository-search operation; legacy consumers called GitHub directly.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Decode, parse, map, and retain the search response representation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One decode and JSON parse per successful wire response, bounded by the transport's 16 MiB response cap and the API's 100-result page size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Arbitrary repository-search bodies could not enter this shared transport cache through the query service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Parsing and mapping occur synchronously before the search promise resolves.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct trimmed query, page, sort, and direction combinations after exact-key coalescing; up to 500 retained bodies, each with up to 100 repositories.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One API call creates one request; aggregate active work is capped at 2 per caller and host. Intended picker consumers debounce/throttle input, but successive distinct searches still execute and create distinct cache entries.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold credential resolution is shared as above. Concurrent identical search URLs coalesce. Successful ETagged results are retained in the shared 500-entry LRU under the complete URL, so distinct query/page combinations do not share cache state; failures are not negative-cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed `etag: true`, full-URL cache keys, retained raw response bodies, count-only LRU bound, and type-ahead consumer behavior are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual retained bytes depend on how many searches complete, result density, and repository metadata size; the full-body retention and 500 distinct-key ceiling are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cache-lifecycle regression: high-cardinality search inputs populate a long-lived count-bounded cache with large obsolete result bodies, increasing retained memory and GC pressure.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files. The new APIs avoid automatic pagination and inherit bounded queue concurrency/coalescing. One medium cache-lifecycle issue was submitted for retaining every distinct repository search response in the shared ETag LRU.
